issue.body:
## Summary
`worker/public` appears to be stale checked-in frontend build output, while the active frontend deployment path is Cloudflare Pages from `dist`.

## Why this needs investigation
- The repo currently points frontend deployment at `dist` via Pages.
- Worker configs and runtime appear API-only.
- `worker/public` duplicates built frontend artifacts and creates review noise, but an undocumented external deploy step or manual workflow could still depend on it.

## Goal
Confirm whether any active deployment path, CI job, or operational process still depends on `worker/public`.

If nothing depends on it:
- remove `worker/public` from the repo
- remove any workflow that regenerates or updates it
- update docs so the frontend artifact and deployment path have a single source of truth

If something does depend on it:
- document that dependency explicitly
- explain why the artifact belongs in this repo
- make the ownership and generation path consistent with the rest of the deployment architecture

## Definition of done
There is one documented, authoritative frontend artifact path and `worker/public` is either removed or justified.

issue.title: fix: add blob: to media-src CSP for proxied video previews
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds `blob:` to the `media-src` CSP directive in `index.html`. Proxied restricted media creates blob URLs that `media-src 'self' https:` was blocking. `img-src` and `connect-src` already allow `blob:` -- this aligns `media-src`.

## Motivation

Restricted video content loads through the admin media proxy (`/api/media-proxy/{sha256}`), which fetches from the media server's admin endpoint and creates a blob URL for the `<video>` element. CSP was blocking the blob URL, causing the AlertTriangle fallback instead of the video preview.

## Related Issue

- Relates to moderation media preview workflow

## Validation

- [x] `npm run test`
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vite build`
- [x] No worker code changed

## Manual Test Plan / Notes

- [x] Playwright network capture: proxy requests return 200, no CSP console errors for blob URLs
- [x] Deployed to production Pages, opened NS-sexualContent report with age-restricted video -- video preview renders correctly through proxy chain
- [x] Non-restricted media still loads directly (verified on NS-spam report with external video)

## Visuals / API Examples

- [x] No visual change (CSP header only; video rendering was broken before, now works)

## Public Artifact Review

- [x] Titles, descriptions, branch names, and screenshots avoid partner, customer, brand, campaign, or other sensitive external names unless explicitly approved

issue.title: feat(reports): add NS-prefixed CATEGORY_LABELS for mobile report reasons
issue.body:
## Problem

divine-mobile is adding NIP-32 l/L tags to Kind 1984 events to restore app-level report categorization (see divinevideo/divine-mobile#3488). The l tags use the format `NS-{reason.name}` (e.g., `NS-csam`, `NS-violence`, `NS-harassment`).

`getReportCategory()` already reads l tags as a fallback, but `CATEGORY_LABELS` only maps `NS-csam` and `NS-ai-generated`. The remaining 8 mobile reason names with NS- prefix are unmapped and would display as raw strings.

## Solution

Add 8 new entries to `CATEGORY_LABELS` in `src/lib/constants.ts`:

- `NS-spam` -> Spam
- `NS-harassment` -> Harassment
- `NS-violence` -> Violence
- `NS-sexualContent` -> Sexual Content
- `NS-copyright` -> Copyright
- `NS-falseInformation` -> Misinformation
- `NS-aiGenerated` -> AI Generated (note: camelCase, distinct from existing `NS-ai-generated` which is divine-web's kebab-case format)
- `NS-other` -> Other

## Related

- Blocked by: divinevideo/divine-mobile#3488 (mobile must emit the tags first for testing)
- Design spec: support-trust-safety `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-report-reason-label-tags-design.md`

review.body:
The `index.html` CSP change looks correct: adding `blob:` to `media-src` matches how restricted media is loaded through `/api/media-proxy/{sha256}` and then rendered from a blob URL in the media preview code.

I am requesting changes because this PR currently includes unrelated `worker/public` rebuild output in a separate commit (`16df851`). Based on the repo’s current deployment path, the frontend is deployed from `dist` via Cloudflare Pages, while the worker is API-only. That makes the `worker/public` churn out of scope for this fix and it obscures review of the actual shipping change.

Please update this PR to:
1. Drop the `worker/public` rebuild commit so the diff is only the one-line CSP change in `index.html`.
2. Complete the two unchecked manual validations in the PR description:
- reload a report with restricted video content and confirm the preview renders
- verify non-restricted media still loads normally

Follow-up cleanup is tracked in #54, so that debt does not need to block this fix once the PR is narrowed and the manual checks are done.

comment.body:
This reusable workflow is pinned to the floating `v1` tag. Combined with the `pull_request_target` trigger above, anything that gets pushed to `v1` in the future runs here against PR events, including PRs from forks. The `permissions: pull-requests: read` block keeps the blast radius small (no write tokens in scope), so this is a hardening suggestion rather than a block. GitHub's Actions security guidance recommends pinning third-party actions and reusable workflows by full commit SHA to defend against tag-movement:

```suggestion
    uses: VeryGoodOpenSource/very_good_workflows/.github/workflows/semantic_pull_request.yml@<commit-sha>  # v1
```

Replace `<commit-sha>` with the SHA that `v1` currently points to; the trailing comment keeps the human-readable version visible.

issue.title: feat(reports): add NS-prefixed CATEGORY_LABELS for mobile report reasons
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds NS-prefixed CATEGORY_LABELS entries for the `NS-{reason.name}` format that divine-mobile emits via NIP-32 l tags. 9 direct mobile aliases plus 2 defensive kebab-case aliases for confirmed multi-word variants (NS-sexual-content, NS-false-information). Ensures report category chips display correctly for mobile-originated reports.

## Motivation

The March NIP-56 compliance change on divine-mobile collapsed 9 app-level report reasons to 7 standard types, losing the distinction for relay-manager's category chips. divine-mobile added NIP-32 l/L tags to restore this (divinevideo/divine-mobile#3492). This PR adds the corresponding label mappings so the chips render correctly. No logic changes -- `getReportCategory()` already reads `l` tags as fallback.

## Related Issue

- Closes #49

## Validation

- [x] `npm run test` (tsc + eslint + vitest + vite build all pass)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vite build`
- [x] No worker code changed

## Manual Test Plan / Notes

- [x] Category chips render correctly for all 9 NS-* labels (verified via nak + iOS simulator)
- [x] Kebab-case aliases verified against divine-mobile#3492 wire format

## Visuals / API Examples

- [x] No visual change (lookup table entries only; chips already render, just lacked these mappings)

## Public Artifact Review

- [x] Titles, descriptions, branch names, and screenshots avoid partner, customer, brand, campaign, or other sensitive external names unless explicitly approved

comment.body: @NotThatKindOfDrLiz thanks for the review. @rabble this is ready on our end whenever you want to sign off.

review.body: LGTM. Verified this against divine-mobile#3492 and the current relay-manager diff is in the right shape: the 8 emitted mobile `NS-*` labels are covered, `NS-csam` remains wired for high-priority handling, and the added kebab-case aliases are a low-risk hardening step for multi-word labels.\n\nThe focused Vitest coverage on `CATEGORY_LABELS` and `getReportCategory()` is the right amount of contract protection for this repo. Merge is fine from my side once the requested sign-off lands.

comment.body:
@mbradley thanks for the verification — a few things to square away before merge:

1. **PR # in the description is stale.** The body links `divine-mobile#3488` but you confirmed `#3492` is what actually merged. Mind updating the body so the merge trail is correct?

2. **Kebab/camel alias coverage is asymmetric.** The inline comment I added at `constants.ts:8-9` says "keep both kebab- and camel-case aliases where clients already differ on wire values," but this PR only ships camelCase for `NS-sexualContent` and `NS-falseInformation`. Only `NS-aiGenerated` has both forms (because `NS-ai-generated` was already there). You cited `useModeration.ts:264-265` from divine-web — can you confirm what divine-web actually emits on the wire for those two? If it's kebab-case, those reports will render as raw strings until we add the aliases.

3. **divine-web producer path isn't covered by the e2e.** Your test plan exercises mobile + synthetic `nak` events. The PR body lists `divine-web#280` as part of the alignment — was that intentionally out of scope for this verification, or should we get a parallel check there before merging?

4. **CSAM naming question (`divine-mobile#3489`) still open.** `NS-csam` is fine today (already in `HIGH_PRIORITY_CATEGORIES`), but if the mobile naming question lands on a different wire value we'll need a follow-up. Worth tracking.

Once 1-3 are squared, I'm comfortable taking this out of draft and pinging Rabble.

issue.title: feat(reports): add NS-prefixed CATEGORY_LABELS for mobile report reasons
issue.body:
## Problem

divine-mobile is adding NIP-32 l/L tags to Kind 1984 events to restore app-level report categorization (see divinevideo/divine-mobile#3488). The l tags use the format `NS-{reason.name}` (e.g., `NS-csam`, `NS-violence`, `NS-harassment`).

`getReportCategory()` already reads l tags as a fallback, but `CATEGORY_LABELS` only maps `NS-csam` and `NS-ai-generated`. The remaining 8 mobile reason names with NS- prefix are unmapped and would display as raw strings.

## Solution

Add 8 new entries to `CATEGORY_LABELS` in `src/lib/constants.ts`:

- `NS-spam` -> Spam
- `NS-harassment` -> Harassment
- `NS-violence` -> Violence
- `NS-sexualContent` -> Sexual Content
- `NS-copyright` -> Copyright
- `NS-falseInformation` -> Misinformation
- `NS-aiGenerated` -> AI Generated (note: camelCase, distinct from existing `NS-ai-generated` which is divine-web's kebab-case format)
- `NS-other` -> Other

## Related

- Blocked by: divinevideo/divine-mobile#3488 (mobile must emit the tags first for testing)
- Design spec: support-trust-safety `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-report-reason-label-tags-design.md`

issue.title: feat(zendesk): attribute moderator identity in ticket assignee sync
issue.body:
## Context

When relay admin auto-solves a Zendesk ticket after a moderation action, it sets the assignee to the API user because there's no per-moderator identity in the current auth flow. All moderators share a single admin signing key.

## When Keycast Teams is integrated

Once Keycast Teams is wired into relay admin auth, each moderator authenticates with their own divine.video identity. The relay admin will know who is logged in, even though moderation actions are signed with the shared moderation@ key.

## What to do

- Pass the authenticated moderator's identity through to `syncZendeskAfterAction` and `addZendeskInternalNote`
- Use it as the `assignee_email` when solving tickets, so Zendesk reflects who actually took the action
- Update the decision log to record the individual moderator identity alongside the shared signing key

## Depends on

- Keycast Teams integrated with relay admin auth
- Per-moderator divine.video identities established

comment.body:
@mbradley @NotThatKindOfDrLiz Hey!

I did a deep pass on issue #41 and reviewed the relevant flows in divine-relay-manager, plus related auth/identity context in keycast and divine-web. I used AI for this to collect as much information as possible for manual analysis.

What I’ve confirmed so far:

- Relay Admin currently does not have reliable per-moderator identity in the main moderation flow.
- Moderation actions are still signed with the shared moderation@ key, so syncZendeskAfterAction does not consistently know which human took the action.
- On Zendesk resolve, currently set assignee_email to the technical ZENDESK_EMAIL, so tickets get assigned to the API user, not the actual moderator.
- Some moderation actions go through the RPC path, and that path also needs to be included for identity + Zendesk consistency.

I'd be happy to help with this task, but I'd like to confirm a few things with you to avoid a PR with a partial solution:

1) Is the target source of truth for moderator identity Keycast/Divine identity (email), rather than CF Access identity headers?
2) Is Keycast Teams integration for Relay Admin auth already available for this workflow, or still a blocker/dependency?
3) If a moderator doesn't have a valid Zendesk agent account, what should the fallback be: assign to API user, skip auto-resolve, or something else?
4) Should this change cover all moderation action paths (including /api/relay-rpc), or only the /api/moderate path?
5) For the decision log, do you want explicit separate fields for shared signer and human moderator identities (e.g., shared_signing_pubkey, moderator_email, moderator_pubkey)?
6) Should the current resolution action list remain as is, or do we want to review which actions auto-resolve tickets as part of this task?

I think this could be a two-step process:

Step 1: Identity plumbing + audit logging everywhere
Step 2: Zendesk assignee behavior once account mapping is confirmed

What do you think?
